To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bootstrapped hindsight experience replay (BHER) is an efficient and effective way to solve sparse reward tasks, in which we explicitly leverage the diversity and uncertainty of multiple heads to learn with relabelled goals.
bootstrapping and prioritizing hindsight experience replay (BHER) can achieve state-of-art results in many continuous control tasks.

(1) bootstrapped version of HER can significantly improve the performance in goal-conditioned tasks; (2) the uncertainty of estimated Q-values can be used to improve the performance of HER; (3) exploiting lower uncertainty samples will further improve the data efficiency of HER.

the following questions: (1) What is the difference between bootstrapping and hindsight experiences in the goal-conditioned setting? (2) How to effectively utilize hindsight experiences? (3) How to balance exploration and exploitation in hindsight experiences?

, for goal-conditioned tasks, the agent can learn more effectively with lower uncertainty data, and it may not be necessary to learn with the highest uncertainty data as the common belief in Q-learning.
